answer: One strong defense is stake-bonded reputation: before an agent can trade, it locks a refundable deposit — think of copper tokens held in escrow — tied to a single long-lived identity. Good behavior slowly builds trust, like water collecting in a desert oasis, while fraud slashes the deposit and burns the reputation. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity separately, and crossing the canyon between one cheap fake and a trusted trader means paying the full bond each time, so mass fakery becomes ruinously expensive while honest newcomers pay only once.
